extension.description: Dispatch coding tasks from your Claude Code session to worker accounts in parallel — other Claude Code accounts, plus opt-in Codex, Cursor and Antigravity — with quota-aware failover, live plan usage, a Team view of live sessions and a dashboard. Unofficial.

viewsWelcome.workers:
No worker accounts yet.
A worker is another account — on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Antigravity — that implements what your main session designs and verifies.
[Add Worker Account](command:claudeCodeOrchestrator.addWorker)
[Import Existing Claude Directories](command:claudeCodeOrchestrator.importWorkers)
Then set up this workspace so that your Claude Code session can dispatch.
[Update Workspace Setup](command:claudeCodeOrchestrator.updateWorkspaceSetup)
viewsWelcome.team.off:
Teammate mode runs a live team of coding agents on your worker accounts — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Antigravity — each in its own git worktree and branch, led by your Claude Code session with the cco team_* commands. It is experimental and off by default.
[Turn On Teammate Mode](command:claudeCodeOrchestrator.teamModeTurnOn)
This view also lists the live Claude Code sessions working here. Session workers appear when Mesh Mode is on.
[Open Settings](command:claudeCodeOrchestrator.openSettings)
To put a worker account into a native agent team, install the team proxy agent.
[Install Team Proxy Agent](command:claudeCodeOrchestrator.installTeamAgent)
One-shot workers on Codex, Cursor or Antigravity appear under Dispatched Tasks, not here.
viewsWelcome.team.on:
Teammate mode is on. There is no team in this workspace yet.
Start one from your Claude Code session with cco team_create <team file> (cco help team_create shows the file format). Its members, task board and messages then appear here.
This view also lists the live Claude Code sessions working here. Session workers appear when Mesh Mode is on.
[Open Settings](command:claudeCodeOrchestrator.openSettings)
To put a worker account into a native agent team, install the team proxy agent.
[Install Team Proxy Agent](command:claudeCodeOrchestrator.installTeamAgent)
One-shot workers on Codex, Cursor or Antigravity appear under Dispatched Tasks, not here.
viewsWelcome.tasks:
No dispatched tasks to show.
Ask your Claude Code session to fan work out with dispatch_tasks — each task appears here as it starts.
[Open Dashboard](command:claudeCodeOrchestrator.openDashboard)
Tasks from other workspaces are hidden by default.
[Toggle Task Scope](command:claudeCodeOrchestrator.toggleTaskScope)
viewsWelcome.workerHistory:
No finished session-worker dispatches in this workspace.
When Mesh Mode is on, every finished dispatch is kept here with its result branch, and a branch that is not merged yet is flagged.

walkthrough.step.meshMode.title: Try session workers — Mesh Mode (experimental)
walkthrough.step.meshMode.description:
Run each dispatch as a persistent background session in its own git worktree: message it from your own session with SendMessage, attach to it from the Team view, and merge its branch when it passes. Needs Claude Code 2.1.283 or newer. Turn on the claudeCodeOrchestrator.meshMode setting to switch it on.
[Open Settings](command:claudeCodeOrchestrator.openSettings)
configuration.title: Claude Code Orchestrator
config.workerPermissionMode.description: --permission-mode for dispatched workers. A dispatched worker runs unattended and cannot answer a permission prompt, so a mode that asks ('default') stalls on its first edit. Session workers (Mesh Mode) never run in 'bypassPermissions': they start in 'acceptEdits' instead. Applies to Claude Code workers only: a worker on another vendor's CLI has a permission mode of its own ("Set Permission Mode" on the worker).
config.claudePath.description: The Claude Code CLI to run: a command name such as `claude` (looked up on PATH) or an absolute path. A relative path or one starting with '~' is not used: the default `claude` is used instead and you are told. Read from your User settings only — a workspace value is ignored.
config.quotaCooldownMinutes.description: Minutes a worker account sits out after a quota/rate-limit error before dispatches are routed to it again.
config.workerTimeoutMinutes.description: Minutes a dispatched worker may run before it is terminated. Deep tasks (contract-critical implementation, adversarial review) routinely exceed 30 minutes; a task killed here loses its unwritten work. A single task can override this with the dispatch tool's timeout_minutes argument.
config.assetPacks.description: Additional asset-pack directories ('~' allowed). Each pack mirrors the .claude/ layout — skills/, agents/, commands/, output-styles/ — and its assets become available in 'Manage Workspace Assets'. Point this at a clone of a private asset repo to keep personal assets out of the public extension.
config.assetAutoSync.description: On startup, refresh assets enabled in this workspace when their pack content changed. Files you have edited by hand are never overwritten — the Asset Manager shows them as 'customized', with a diff against the pending pack version.
config.frontierWorkerDispatch.enumDescri: Reject worker dispatches that request the frontier tier (fable), with a fall-back hint — recommended when that tier bills per use instead of drawing from the subscription quota. Dispatches of every other model are unaffected.
Allow worker dispatches to request the frontier tier (fable). Enable only if you accept the cost (separate quota or pay-per-use billing, depending on the plan).
config.frontierWorkerDispatch.descriptio: Billing guard over WHICH MODEL may be dispatched: it governs only the frontier tier (fable). 'block' (default) makes the dispatch server reject those dispatches and steer the orchestrator to opus + ultrathink. This setting does NOT prevent overage billing for other models — a dispatch of any model can still spend real money past an exhausted plan window; that is controlled by overageWorkerDispatch.
config.meshMode.description: EXPERIMENTAL. Turn on session workers (Mesh Mode): each dispatched task runs as a persistent background session (`claude --bg`) instead of a one-shot worker. In a git workspace the worker edits in its own worktree and branch, created from your current HEAD commit — it sees every commit on the current branch and nothing uncommitted. Requires Claude Code >= 2.1.283 on macOS or Linux. A session worker is a peer of your own session: steer it with SendMessage, using the name on the `peer:` line of the dispatch result, and find it in the Team view to attach, read its logs or stop it. Dispatch itself is unchanged — same dispatch_task / dispatch_tasks tools, results, timeouts, cancellation and failover. Tasks dispatched with detach still run as one-shot workers, and when session workers cannot be used (an older CLI, or an account that has not trusted this workspace) the dispatch falls back to a one-shot worker and says so in its result. Off by default.
config.meshMaxLiveWorkers.description: EXPERIMENTAL. Maximum number of session workers with a dispatch still in flight. A dispatch past the cap is REFUSED, not queued: it fails with a worker_cap error naming this limit. Parked workers — their dispatch has finished and they only stay attachable — do not count. Let running dispatches finish before a larger fan-out, or raise this number. Only takes effect when Mesh Mode is on.
config.meshHistoryLimit.description: EXPERIMENTAL. Maximum number of finished session-worker dispatches kept in the Worker History view before the oldest are dropped. Integer, default 50, minimum 1. Only takes effect when Mesh Mode is on.
config.workerPermissionMode.enumDescript: File edits are accepted automatically. Recommended.
Claude Code's auto mode decides which actions may run without asking.
Never asks: an action the account's permission rules do not already allow is denied.
Plan mode: the worker analyzes and proposes but does not change files.
Asks before edits and commands. An unattended worker cannot answer, so it stalls.
Skips permission checks (one-shot workers only). A session worker starts in acceptEdits instead: a bypass session cannot exchange messages with an orchestrator that is not in bypass mode.
config.overageWorkerDispatch.enumDescrip: Never assign work to a quota-exhausted worker, even when that account has extra usage enabled — dispatch never spends money past a plan window.
Exhausted workers with extra usage enabled may be used as a last resort. Those dispatches bill real money against the account's monthly cap.
config.overageWorkerDispatch.description: Billing guard for overage (extra-credit) dispatches. 'block' (default): the dispatch server never assigns work to a quota-exhausted worker, even when that account has extra usage enabled — dispatch never spends money past a plan window. 'allow': exhausted workers with extra usage enabled may be used as a last resort; those dispatches bill real money against the account's monthly cap. Independent of frontierWorkerDispatch, which only controls the frontier tier (fable).
config.sessionKeepalive.description: Send one minimal Claude request (haiku model) per subscription account per 24h to keep OAuth sessions fresh. Spends a negligible amount of plan usage. Off by default; recovery from an already-expired login is the Re-login command.

config.providerUsagePolling.description: Ask other vendors' CLIs for plan usage. When on (the default), every usage refresh — at startup, every 5 minutes, and on "Refresh Account Usage" — also asks each worker account that runs on another vendor's CLI (Codex, Cursor, Antigravity) for a usage reading. Where the vendor provides one, that is a request sent from this machine to the vendor's usage service; a helper process reads the login the vendor's CLI already stored here to make it, and the extension stores and shows no token. Turn this off to stop those requests: such accounts then show "no usage reading", their login state is still checked through the CLI, and dispatch is unaffected. Claude Code accounts are not governed by this setting.

config.teamMode.description: EXPERIMENTAL. Turn on Teammate mode: your Claude Code session can lead a team of coding agents — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Antigravity worker accounts — each in its own git worktree and branch, coordinating through messages and a shared task board, with the `cco team_*` commands. The Team view shows every team of this workspace and lets you message, pause, stop or take over its members. macOS and Linux only. Turned off while a team runs, the team continues; only creating a team or adding a member is refused. Off by default.
config.teamMaxMembers.description: EXPERIMENTAL. Maximum number of members in one team, stopped members included. Integer, default 6, 1 to 8. Only takes effect when Teammate mode is on.
config.teamMaxRunningTurns.description: EXPERIMENTAL. Maximum number of team member turns running at once in one Claude Code session. Turns do not take dispatch slots. Integer, default 4, 1 to 16. Only takes effect when Teammate mode is on.
config.teamTurnTimeoutMinutes.descriptio: EXPERIMENTAL. Minutes one team member turn may run before it is stopped. Integer, 5 to 240. Not set (the default): the value of workerTimeoutMinutes. Only takes effect when Teammate mode is on.
config.teamTurnsPerMemberPerHour.descrip: EXPERIMENTAL. Maximum number of turns one team member may start per hour; past it the member waits. Integer, default 20, 1 to 240. Only takes effect when Teammate mode is on.
config.teamTurnsPerDay.description: EXPERIMENTAL. Maximum number of turns per team per day; past it the team waits until tomorrow. Integer, default 300, 10 to 5000. Only takes effect when Teammate mode is on.
config.teamCursorForce.description: EXPERIMENTAL. Cursor teammates run with `--force` (commands run without approval). Off by default: Cursor teammates then edit files but may not reach their team tools on every turn. Only takes effect when Teammate mode is on.
config.teamAgySkipPermissions.descriptio: EXPERIMENTAL. Antigravity teammates run with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` — needed for their team tools; every command then runs without approval. Off by default: Antigravity teammates then run turns-only (they report at the end of each turn and cannot use the team tools). Only takes effect when Teammate mode is on.
